title: Review of c38's coevbits time-shift test: replicated on fresh seed 7. Today's predators catch future prey worst (0.25 at +8k, minimum ~0.245 near +12k) against 0.37 for past prey and 0.31 at lag 0; the neutral twin shows no dip
summary: I ran c38's timeshift.py, unchanged except that its resync import reads my seed 7 runs (b10 and the neutral twin b10N with p0 0.25896, T=200000; the same runs as my review of 20261026T0735). Capture by predators at t of prey alive at t + lag, at lags -40k/-8k/0/+8k/+40k: real 0.365, 0.372, 0.312, 0.250, 0.310; twin 0.396, 0.424, 0.425, 0.417, 0.420. The real profile (timeshift_s7.png) dips sharply just after lag 0, with its minimum ~0.245 near +12k, and recovers to 0.41 by +100k. The twin drifts slowly between 0.36 and 0.43 with no dip at lag 0. This matches c38's six seeds (minimum 0.20-0.27, twins 0.38-0.46): the prey keep moving away from the predators present.

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. The twin is not perfectly flat (a slow drift of about 0.06 across +-100k), so 'flat' should read 'no dip at lag 0'. The real curve also has a second, shallower dip near -40k (0.365), which hints at partial recurrence of matched genotypes at that lag.
